_sources.classes: Class from causes, not latitude bands: site warm-season temperature = sea-level warm season (altitude-zones.json) minus the lapse rate times elevation. Below 0 C is ice (Ohmura et al. 1992), below the 6.4 C tree-line temperature is tundra where the tree line itself is at sea level and rock in mountains (Koerner & Paulsen 2004; Matt's rule: high land gets no plants). Above it, the planet sample's vegetation weight (0..1, a moisture proxy) splits desert, prairie and forest at the thresholds the viewer already uses (coverKind.ts, 0.28 and 0.62).
_sources.boreal: Closed boreal stands are often 1,000-3,000 stems/ha (already cited in coverKind.ts) [verify]; mature spruce canopy 10-25 m [verify].
_sources.prairie: Counts are shrub or bunch clumps a billboard can stand for, not grass tillers. Game calibration.
_sources.desert: Open shrubland, a few hundred to about a thousand shrubs/ha, 1-3 m (creosote-type scrub) [verify]. Game calibration.
_sources.tundra: Dwarf shrubs 0.1-0.5 m [verify]. The viewer places no billboard; the count is for the ground texture.
_sources.tropical: Lowland tropical moist forest: often 400-700 stems/ha over 10 cm DBH, canopy 25-45 m (RAINFOR plots, e.g. Phillips et al. 1998) [verify]. Class needs vegetation >= veg_prairie_below and a site annual mean >= tropical_mean_C (North 1975 mean minus the lapse rate); 22 C is a calibration near the Koeppen A-climate edge [verify].
_sources.wetland: Northern peatland (bog and fen with open black spruce and tamarack), as in the Hudson Bay lowland: a few hundred stems/ha, 3-10 m [verify]. Class needs prairie-band vegetation, |lat| >= wetland_lat_min and height below wetland_below_m: a cold flat lowland with that much green is muskeg, not grass. Both numbers are calibration [verify].
_sources.note: Every range is labelled calibration, not a census (PROJECT-RULES 5 and 7). A place picks a value inside its range from a hash of lat/lon, so the same place always returns the same row.
